strongest_angle: Analysis of National Centers for Environmental Information data from October 2026 showing that global ocean surface temperature departures broke all-time monthly records for a fifth consecutive month.

key_facts.fact: The National Centers for Environmental Information reported that October 2026 global ocean surface temperature departure reached 1.14°C above average, setting an all-time high for any month.
Mercator Ocean International stated that global sea surface temperatures between 60°S and 60°N averaged 21.01°C in October 2026, surpassing the previous record set in 2023.
According to the National Centers for Environmental Information, 75 percent of the global ocean showed above average mean sea surface temperatures in October 2026.
Yale Climate Connections reported that October 2026 was Earth's warmest October since modern record-keeping began in 1850 according to NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information.
